text:
Alex: quick heads-up — noticed a p95 regression on the canary after the partial-quant rollout (embed excluded)
Priya: oof, how big?
Alex: from ~82ms -> ~135ms on gen-2 perf harness for batch size 4, seq_len 256
Sam: did the kv hit rate change? that often explains jump
Alex: yes, KV cache hit dropped ~12% on mixed workload — looks like more kernel switches during autoreg
Jordan: any logs from kernel selector? might be flapping between fp8-packed and int8-fused
Alex: here's the snippet from runtime profiler:
```
kernel_switches: 18 -> 47
avg_dispatch_latency_ms: 0.8 -> 1.9
kv_lookup_miss_delta: +12%
hot_kernel: int4-llm (40%), fp8-packed (30%), int8-fused (30%)
```
Priya: hmm. we excluded embeddings/lm_head from quant, right? that can change token distribution drastically
Sam: can you paste the batch routing policy? maybe batching heuristic now groups sequences that trigger different kernel paths
Alex: routing config (canary):
```
quant_policy:
  per_layer: partial
  exclude: [embedding, lm_head]
kernel_preference: [fused-int8, fp8-packed, fallback-fp32]
batch_split_ms: 8
```
Jordan: I suspect the exclude makes early tokens use fp32 path then switch mid-sequence when content hits quantized layers -> KV cache entries created under fp32 keys, causing misses when later calls hit the quantized kernel key
Priya: sounds plausible. could also be calibration thresholds shifting activation ranges -> different kernel chosen by compiler at runtime
perf-bot: small probe run scheduled on stg with seq=128 bs=8, will post results in ~5m
Sam: short-term mitigation: raise batch_split_ms to 20 to reduce intra-batch heterogeneity and force same kernel per batch
Alex: tried bumping to 20 locally — p95 improved to ~95ms but throughput down 8%
Jordan: that's acceptable for canary; we need root cause though
Priya: let's capture kernel decision traces per-token (cheap sampling) and KV key namespace + kernel tag for each cache entry
Alex: working on adding trace: will instrument kv write with kernel_tag + layer_id
Sam: also run microbench of quantized vs fp32 kernels for the sensitive attention layers — do a per-layer forward latency sweep
Priya: I can run sensitivity calibration too: run layerwise recalib with small eval set to detect layers where FP->INT quant causes activation shift
Jordan: good. if certain middle transformer layers are sensitive, mark them as "pin_fp32" in policy
Alex: one more thing — saw a small increase in GPU memcpy contention when switching kernels (cudaStream syncs). logs:
```
memcpy_sync_waits: +22
stream_stalls: +15
```
Sam: that explains part of latency spike
Priya: plan: (1) enable per-token kernel tracing (Alex), (2) run layer latency sweep (Sam), (3) run recalib sensitivity (Priya), (4) canary tweak batch_split and kernel preference to fused-int8-first (Jordan)
Alex: I'll open a short-lived canary branch with tracing and a minimal dashboard panel for kernel flaps
perf-bot: canary probe finished: p95=102ms bs=8 seq=128; kv_hit ~-7% vs baseline. logs uploaded to /perf/canaries/1899998765
Jordan: thanks. let's sync after traces — tentative sync in 30m
Alex: cool — ping me in thread when you have microbench results :thumbsup:
Priya: I'll upload recalib outputs to the same path
Sam: adding short replay script to repro: `./bench --model=xl-small --quant=partial --exclude=embed,lm_head --trace-kernel`
Alex: perfect. if anyone sees a quick win before the sync, drop it here
Priya: noted — also checking optimizer flags for kernel selector heuristics (heuristic smoothing window)
Jordan: if we end up marking 2-3 sensitive layers as FP-only, it's a cheap fix and low perf penalty
Alex: agree. ok, back to work — will update in thread when traces are in
